candidates.name: Bari Cathedral
candidates.content: A Roman church even older than St. Nicolas', though later refurbished in baroque style, and equally interesting.

candidates.name: Church of Santa Chiara

candidates.name: Chiesa di Sant’Anna
candidates.content: St. Anna Church was built between 1246-1247 as a synagogue, known as “Scola Grande”. It was later converted into a Christian Church and entrusted to the Confraternity of St. Anna. Finally, in 2009, the Church became a museum.Its h

candidates.name: Basilica of Saint Nicholas
candidates.content: This romanic church with a gold ceiling and a crypt contains many medieval attractions, including the magnificent cathedra of Bishop Elias.

candidates.name: Castello normanno-svevo
candidates.content: The symbolic fortress of the city: built in the 12th century, destroyed and then rebuilt during the 13th century by Frederick II.

candidates.name: Teatro Petruzzelli
candidates.content: The largest theatre of the city and the fourth Italian theatre by size. Its season feature high quality productions of prose, opera, ballet and classical music.

candidates.name: Black Lounge bar
candidates.content: Bar at the exit from Giardino Garibaldi.

candidates.content: An old and very informal restaurant in the old town. Traditional, non-posh cuisine. Simple four-course menu for about €15.

december.text: Bari is composed of four urban sections. In the northern city area, there is the Old Town (Bari Vecchia) between two modern harbours, with the Basilica of Saint Nicholas, the Cathedral of San Sabino (1035–1171) and the Hohenstaufen Castle built for Frederick II, which is now also a major nightlife district.
